audit_result.proof_trace: The authorization code replay prevention relies on two separate async RPC calls: `get_authorization_code` (L70-73) and `delete_authorization_code` (L83), with an `await` yield point between them. Node.js yields at each `await`, allowing a second concurrent request to fetch the same code before the first request deletes it — both requests then hold the `authCode` object in memory and proceed to generate JWT tokens. The return value of `delete_authorization_code` at L83 is not checked, so neither request is blocked even if the delete is a no-op.
audit_result.attack_scenario: Attacker triggers two concurrent POST /oauth/token requests with the same authorization code; both `get_authorization_code` RPCs succeed before either `delete_authorization_code` executes, yielding two valid 30-day JWT access tokens from a single code exchange.

PROP-kintai-v3-st-asm-002.text: PKCE flow in Supabase Auth must reject replayed authorization codes.
